1. By O1, the native structure of a protein is uniquely defined as the global minimum of its free energy landscape. [O1]

3. When aligning the native structure to itself, an optimal superposition exists where every residue is superimposed exactly on itself, yielding \( d_i = 0 \) for all i. [O4]
4. Substituting \( d_i = 0 \) into the TM-score formula gives each term as \( rac{1}{1+0} = 1 \), and the average over L residues is \( rac{1}{L} \sum_{i=1}^{L} 1 = 1 \). Therefore, the TM-score of the native structure with itself is 1. [O4]
5. For any other structure (not the native structure), by O1 it is not the global minimum free energy structure. When optimally aligned to the native structure, at least one residue pair must have a non-zero distance \( d_i &gt; 0 \) because the structures are not identical. [O1, O4]
6. For any residue with \( d_i &gt; 0 \), the term \( rac{1}{1 + (d_i/d_0(L))^2} \) is strictly less than 1. All other terms are at most 1. [O4]
7. Therefore, the sum \( \sum_{i=1}^{L} rac{1}{1 + (d_i/d_0(L))^2} \) is strictly less than L, and the TM-score (the maximum average) is strictly less than 1. [O4]
8. Consequently, for a single protein, the TM-score between its native structure and any other structure is ≤ 1, with equality if and only if the other structure is the native structure itself. [O1, O4]

1. By O1, the native structure of a protein is uniquely defined as the global minimum of its free energy landscape. [O1]
2. By the definition in O4, the TM-score between two structures is computed as the maximum over alignments of the average of terms \( rac{1}{1 + (d_i/d_0(L))^2} \) for each residue pair i, where \( d_i \) is the distance between aligned residues after optimal superposition. [O4]
3. When aligning the native structure to itself, an optimal superposition exists where every residue is superimposed exactly on itself, yielding \( d_i = 0 \) for all i. [O4]
4. Substituting \( d_i = 0 \) into the TM-score formula gives each term as \( rac{1}{1+0} = 1 \), and the average over L residues is \( rac{1}{L} \sum_{i=1}^{L} 1 = 1 \). Therefore, the TM-score of the native structure with itself is 1. [O4]
5. For any other structure (not the native structure), by O1 it is not the global minimum free energy structure. When optimally aligned to the native structure, at least one residue pair must have a non-zero distance \( d_i &gt; 0 \) because the structures are not identical. [O1, O4]
6. For any residue with \( d_i &gt; 0 \), the term \( rac{1}{1 + (d_i/d_0(L))^2} \) is strictly less than 1. All other terms are at most 1. [O4]
7. Therefore, the sum \( \sum_{i=1}^{L} rac{1}{1 + (d_i/d_0(L))^2} \) is strictly less than L, and the TM-score (the maximum average) is strictly less than 1. [O4]
8. Consequently, for a single protein, the TM-score between its native structure and any other structure is ≤ 1, with equality if and only if the other structure is the native structure itself. [O1, O4]
